description: Highway shot through windshield on I-64 West, lush green tree corridor, light traffic. First photo of the fourth solo western road trip — a tradition that started mid-COVID in June 2020 when the itch to drive west hit and the destination turned out to be wherever Independence, CA happened to be.
I-64 West interstate sign for Exit 191 toward Lexington and Charleston, WV. Blue skies, green hills. About 50 miles out.
Serenity (white Subaru Outback) parked outside the hotel in Marion, VA at dusk. Sunset sky with pink and gold clouds over Appalachian hills. Night stop after Day 1.

Mountain Lynx Transit agency sign — blue rectangular sign with leaping lynx logo on a grassy lot with a fleet of vehicles. Leaving Lynx after the Community Transit Supervisor class — the true start of the westbound leg. Senior Training and Transit Operations Specialist at UVA Transit, visiting a peer agency on the way out of town. Of course.
Deer Park water, Red Bull, and a PJ Fresh pizza box laid out on Serenity's hood at a truck stop at sunset. A semi-truck visible behind. The real Day 3 dinner.
Steel truss bridge silhouetted against deep blue twilight sky, approaching from the highway. River visible below.
Industrial complex reflected in glassy Ohio River at dusk, shot from a bridge. Multiple tall stacks with lights. Small boat wake in the foreground.
Highway approach into Peoria. Brown tourist sign for Peoria Riverfront Museum and Caterpillar Visitors Center at Exit 93. FedEx trucks on the shoulder.
Semi hauling a massive wind turbine blade westbound on I-80, shot from the driver window with the side mirror visible. Iowa farm fields in the background. The scale of this thing.
Highway sign for Exit 11B: Rock Island Arsenal / Riverfront. Brown and green signs against blue sky with light traffic.
Mississippi River sign on the bridge approach. Blue sky, the blue arch bridge visible ahead to the left. Iowa-side cityscape in the distance.
Looking across the Mississippi from the bridge. Wide river view, no buildings visible — just the far bank and open water. Shot over the concrete bridge barrier wall.
Full view of the blue steel arch bridge from the roadway. Bright blue sky, single truck visible ahead.
'THE PEOPLE OF IOWA WELCOME YOU — Fields of Opportunities' welcome sign on an overhead gantry just past the Mississippi. Exit 8 sign for Rockingham Rd visible to the right.
Iowa 80 World's Largest Truck Stop sign — globe logo with red arrow, Truckomat sign below, Wendy's and DQ logos. Shot from highway passing by.
Second angle of Iowa 80 sign, this time with Caribou Coffee and BP logos visible on the taller pole. Trucks lined up in the background lot.

Riverside Iowa — 'Future Birthplace of Captain James T. Kirk, March 22, 2228' granite marker on a stone base. A planned detour. TNG, DS9, Voyager, Strange New Worlds. You drive two hours off the interstate to see a rock with a future date on it. No apologies.
Street banner on a utility pole: 'RIVERSIDE — Birthplace of Capt. Kirk' with a TOS-era Shatner photo. Grain silo in background.

A model of the USS Enterprise (TOS) mounted on a display pedestal outside a civic building in Riverside, Iowa. Road construction crew and 'No Passing Zone' sign in frame. Kirk's hometown takes the franchise seriously.

Street banner in Riverside, Iowa — utility pole mount with a portrait of Chekov (not Kirk) and 'RIVERSIDE / Where the TREK begins.' Grain silo and KENT agricultural building behind. A car drives past.
'NEBRASKA … the good life — Home of Arbor Day' state welcome sign on overhead gantry. Exit 454 for Henry Doorly Zoo alongside it. White Tesla Model Y in the next lane. Just ahead of Omaha.
'WELCOME TO OMAHA' sign on a stone embankment with a black Union Pacific steam locomotive on display above it. Two flags fly overhead. Construction signs and rain drops on the windshield.
Ominous storm sky over the Nebraska plains. Massive dark cloud formation ahead, I-80 straight and flat, a semi to the right. Classic Great Plains storm approach.

Snow-capped isolated peak (Elk Mountain) rising above open Wyoming plains, with a long wooden snow fence running across the midground. Deep blue sky. Arrived here well after dark, sleeping in the car as usual. Pulled down the windshield sunshade the next morning and this was waiting. The trees and flat farmland were gone. Wyoming had shown up overnight.
Second shot of Elk Mountain, slightly wider angle showing more of the snow fence and the surrounding open rangeland. Shot 5 seconds after the previous.
Layered sedimentary cliff face with a red cap rock rising above I-80 near Rock Springs. A brown tourist sign barely visible ahead. Classic Wyoming high desert.
Twin highway tunnels cut into layered white and tan sedimentary cliffs, with a distinctive tall rock formation on the left. Trucks entering the tunnels.

Highway exit sign: 'Carter / Mountain View — Exit 39, Wyoming 412 & 414'. Flat plains with low badlands in the background. Carter Mountain is also the name of a ridge near Charlottesville, VA — a small coincidence on the road west.
Welcome to Utah sign on I-80 — blue billboard-style sign with skier graphic. Sparse rolling hills, overcast sky.
Snow-capped Wasatch Range peaks visible ahead on I-80 through Utah. A blue minivan with bikes on a hitch carrier in the left lane. Ski runs visible on the slopes.
I-80 causeway over the Great Salt Lake. Water on both sides, mountains in the haze, yellow chevron curve warning sign. The road appears to float on the lake surface.
Second causeway shot, slightly different angle. Water to both sides, distant mountains silhouetted, wispy clouds above.
I-80 heading west through the Bonneville area — dead-flat road ruler-straight to a distant mountain horizon. One car far ahead. Still inside the car; the flats are just beginning.
Tree of Utah sculpture — tall abstract tree with spherical colored orbs as foliage, standing on the salt flat. Mile marker 26 visible. Mountains and snow in the distance.
Bonneville Salt Flats from the pullout — jersey barriers line the road edge, the white expanse stretches to distant mountains. A few tiny figures visible walking on the flat.
On the salt flats — blurry wide shot standing on the surface. Overcast light, vast white plane, mountains barely on the horizon.
Looking straight across the salt flat from ground level — perfect flat white plane, solitary rock in midground, distant mountains barely above the horizon line.
Van Holten's Big Papa Hearty Dill Pickle in a bag, held up for the camera inside the car. Nevada welcome snack. 'One Portly Pickle.'

location: Millers Rest Stop, Esmeralda County, NV (US-95)
description: Millers Rest Stop at sunset — dirt turnout with tire tracks and wooden fence posts, Nevada basin-and-range mountains silhouetted against orange-gold sky. Sagebrush in the foreground. Found by chance. After taking these shots, sat in the trunk, watched the sun finish setting, and had a beer. Perfect temperature, hardly anyone else around. One of those places that wasn't supposed to matter.

location: Millers Rest Stop, Esmeralda County, NV
description: Millers sunset, 2 seconds later — same dirt turnout and fence posts, the orange band at the horizon intensifying as the sun drops behind the mountains.

location: Millers Rest Stop, Esmeralda County, NV
description: Third consecutive sunset frame at Millers, 1 second after the previous. The sky has gone deeper orange, the mountains fully silhouetted.

location: Millers Rest Stop, Esmeralda County, NV
description: Serenity from the front quarter at dusk, Millers Rest Stop. Mountains behind, chain-link fence along the dirt turnout, radio antenna visible on roof. Last direct sunset shot before full dark.

location: Millers Rest Stop, Esmeralda County, NV
description: Night sky attempt at Millers — heavily clouded, deep blue frame with diffuse cloud shapes. A few stars barely visible through gaps. Early in the session.

location: Millers Rest Stop, Esmeralda County, NV
description: Stars emerging at Millers. Dark sky with stars visible and a last glow of sunset or distant town light on the horizon. Mountains silhouetted.

location: Millers Rest Stop, Esmeralda County, NV
description: Clear star field at Millers. Dense stars scattered across the frame. A bright star or planet visible at upper right.

location: Millers Rest Stop, Esmeralda County, NV
description: Stars at Millers — utility pole silhouetted in center, tree on right, bright headlights of a passing vehicle on the right edge. Many stars visible above the dark Nevada desert.

location: Millers Rest Stop, Esmeralda County, NV
description: Best star shot of the session — utility pole, trees, and rest area visible with a static rest area building light flaring on the right (not passing headlights). The Milky Way begins to show. Coming from Charlottesville, had never seen so many stars. Millers sits in one of the darkest pockets in the continental US. The sky was enormous. Everything else was proportionally smaller.

location: Millers Rest Stop, Esmeralda County, NV
description: Stars over Millers — nearly entirely dark sky, very faint stars scattered across frame. Extremely dark conditions.

location: Millers Rest Stop, Esmeralda County, NV
description: Final Millers star shot. Nearly identical to previous. Last image taken at this location before departing. Two hours total at Millers.

Green highway sign reading 'Infinity Highway' with infinity symbol logo, on a two-lane road through tan Nevada hills. Windshield glare from a headlight bulb still in its packaging sitting on the dash. Serenity burned through multiple headlight bulbs on this trip.
Two-lane road through a tall ponderosa pine corridor in the Lassen/Plumas region. Yellow centerline, dense conifers on both sides, no traffic. A quiet morning in the mountains.
A calm mountain lake or reservoir in Plumas/Lassen County — green meadow in the foreground, still water reflecting the forested hillside and rounded mountain behind. Shot from the car.

location: Pacific Coast, Humboldt County, CA — WESTERN TERMINUS
description: Hand holding a dark red-brown water-polished rock with white quartz veining, Pacific Ocean in the background. Overcast sky, dark sand, Humboldt County CA. Proof of passage. The Atlantic is home territory. The Pacific takes eleven days to reach. The continent is actually this wide.

location: Pacific Coast, Humboldt County, CA — WESTERN TERMINUS
description: Pacific Ocean shoreline — dark wet sand, layered white wave crests, flat gray overcast sky. Shot from the water's edge. Four seconds after the rock photo.
Night shot through windshield: a deciduous tree lit up bright green by headlights, with a blinding oncoming light flare on the right. Heading south on I-5 after the coast.

Highway message board in the Sierra Nevada foothills: 'WAGON TRAIN TRAVELING WEST OVER SUMMIT'. Rain-spotted windshield. Driving east at the time — the wagon train (visible shortly after) was heading the other direction.
Steep mountain highway with sheer granite face on the left and burn-scarred hillside on the right. Cars ahead in light traffic. Dirty windshield with glare. Sierra Nevada crossing eastbound.

location: US-395, Mammoth Lakes area, CA (Eastern Sierra)
description: US-395 aimed straight at snow-capped Eastern Sierra peaks, Mammoth area. Two lanes, red snow poles on shoulders, pines on both sides. Mountains still heavily loaded with June snow. This is also the highway Daft Punk used as the spine of Electroma — a detail discovered later, and appreciated.

Vasquez Rocks — close-up of the main tilted sandstone formation. The layered rock thrusts at a steep angle against deep blue sky. Known Trek filming location; got out and walked it. A single scrubby tree grows in a crack. The alien planet looks like Southern California up close.
Sandy valley between the Vasquez Rocks formations — the large tilted slab on the left, darker outcroppings on the right, a dirt road disappearing between them. Deep blue sky.

location: Joshua Tree / Twentynine Palms area, CA
description: Hillside covered in Joshua trees and desert scrub, dry brown grass in foreground. Classic high Mojave desert terrain. Shot from the road.
Two-lane desert road through Joshua tree scrubland — a green 'Flamingo Heights' community sign on the right, a distant car visible ahead, power pole on the left. Deep blue sky.

Serenity parked at a desert campsite near Afton Canyon — all-metal picnic shelter and fire ring on the left, gravel pad, rugged canyon buttes behind. It was 115 degrees. Had planned to spend the night, but the heat drove the decision to keep moving. Serenity was also fighting a damaged water pump that could only keep the coolant from boiling over at high RPMs.

location: Afton Canyon, Mojave National Preserve, CA
description: Driving the Mojave Road through Afton Canyon alongside a moving freight train — tank cars and intermodal containers fill the left side, red canyon walls closing in ahead. The train was traveling with us, not parked. The dirt track barely clears the rails.

location: Mojave Road, Mojave National Preserve, CA
description: 'The Mojave Road Historic Route' NPS interpretive sign — brown panel with route map and history text. Low desert hills behind. The official start of the Soda Lake section. (Image displays rotated; needs 90° CCW correction.)

Serenity parked on a dirt track beside the burned-out metal frame of an off-road vehicle — chassis fully gutted, just skeletal tubing left. Desert scrubland and distant mountains behind. An unexpected find on the Mojave Road.

location: Soda Dry Lake, Mojave National Preserve, CA
description: The Travelers Monument on Soda Dry Lake — a historic rock cairn travelers have been adding stones to since the 1800s, an American flag flying from the top. Standing alone on the blinding white alkali surface. Dark desert mountains on the horizon, deep blue sky.

location: Soda Dry Lake, Mojave National Preserve, CA
description: Driving across Soda Dry Lake on the Mojave Road — the flat white alkali plain extends to all horizons, tire tracks on both sides of the rough trail. Shot from the driver's seat.

location: Soda Dry Lake, Mojave National Preserve, CA
description: Ground-level view of the Soda Dry Lake surface — ridged salt and mineral crust in the foreground, distant desert mountains in golden evening light. The Pacific rock from Humboldt County now sitting on the dashboard.

location: Soda Dry Lake, Mojave National Preserve, CA
description: Looking across the blinding white expanse of Soda Dry Lake toward the nearest mountains — a hazy, shimmering view with distant peaks barely visible above the alkali flat. Shot toward the nearest sign of civilization.

location: Mojave Road / Afton Canyon area, CA
description: Dirt track heading toward a solitary dark volcanic hill across a flat golden basin. Golden hour light, sagebrush and dry grass on both sides. Dashboard visible.

Serenity rear view at sunset — Virginia plates BF3126, car heavily dirt-streaked, sun fully setting behind dark mountains. Low-angle shot, but camera was not on the ground. Had been lost in the desert for the last two hours; the relief of finding pavement again is palpable.
Duplicate of previous shot — alternate processed version of the same frame. Sunset behind Serenity.
Towel folded into elephant shape on a hotel bathroom counter, with miniature toiletries tucked into the folds. The only hotel night of the trip.
Goodsprings Pioneer Saloon — 'PIONEER SALOON' and 'GOODSPRINGS GENERAL STORE' signage on a rustic Old West building, wide gravel lot, desert mountains behind. A motorcycle parked outside.
Inside a large highway novelty/candy store — a UFO prop hangs from the dark industrial ceiling, colorful murals cover the walls including 'CANDY OCEAN' painted prominently. Gift displays below.
Interior of a large highway travel center — a shark-tooth painted aircraft model hangs from the red industrial ceiling. 'ROOMS' and 'BEER CAVE' signs visible. Snack aisles below.
Distance sign for Beaver Dam (½ mile), Littlefield, and Desert Springs (2¼ miles) on a pole. Desert terrain and mountains behind. Speed limit 65. Approaching the Virgin River Gorge corridor.
Exit 8 sign for Beaver Dam and Littlefield on I-15, dark SUV ahead. The rocky terrain of the Virgin River Gorge corridor beginning to close in.
I-15 entering the Virgin River Gorge — rocky grey and brown canyon walls closing in on both sides, a white SUV ahead. One of the most dramatic interstate highway segments in the US.
Still entering the Virgin River Gorge on I-15, 4 seconds after the previous shot — canyon walls beginning to close in, layered dark rock faces on both sides. Not quite in it yet. A car ahead.

location: Virgin River Gorge / St. George, UT
description: Now fully in the Virgin River Gorge — the canyon walls press in close, layered rock faces rising on both sides. A blue directional marker sign ahead.
'Welcome to Utah — Life Elevated' illustrated billboard sign with a red rock arch painting on blue. Just past the state line on I-15, the Virgin River Valley opening up behind.

Utah two-lane highway stretching arrow-straight to the horizon — a stiff windsock fully extended on the right, speed limit 80. Red sandstone plateaus visible in the far distance. UT-24 in Capitol Reef country.
Through a very dirty, bug-splattered windshield — a two-lane road curves between dark canyon walls somewhere in Capitol Reef / Green River country. Shot without cleaning first, clearly.

location: Capitol Reef / Green River area, UT
description: UT-24 threading between towering dark basalt canyon walls — sheer cliff face on the left, bright red rock face on the right, the road disappearing into a slot ahead. Shot through the clean windshield one second after the dirty-windshield frame.

location: Capitol Reef / Green River area, UT
description: Road bursting out from between two jagged dark basalt formations into a stunning painted desert vista — vivid red and orange badlands spread to distant mesas. Deep blue sky. Possibly the most cinematic frame of the trip.

location: Capitol Reef / Green River area, UT
description: One second later — same cinematic rock-gateway scene, slightly wider framing. The road threads between the dark formations into the wide painted desert beyond.

Canyon overlook at dusk near Green River — photographer's shadow visible in the lower left, red sandstone buttes and eroded canyon walls in the middle distance. Deep blue sky. Got out of the car for this one.

Approaching Hole N' The Rock on US-191 — the 'HOLE N THE ROCK' lettering visible on the red sandstone formation ahead, traffic on the two-lane road, red canyon walls flanking the highway. Shot 7 seconds before the closer frame.

Hole N' The Rock on US-191 south of Moab — 'HOLE N THE ROCK' painted in large white letters across the face of a smooth domed sandstone formation. Multiple vehicles and tourist traffic in the lot. Shot from the road passing by.

location: Wilson Arch, UT (US-191 south of Moab)
description: Wilson Arch on US-191 south of Moab — a wide natural sandstone arch framing blue sky, two tiny people visible standing in the opening for scale. A motorcyclist in the foreground. Juniper trees below.
Leaving New Mexico sign — yellow panel on a tan masonry pillar: 'YOU ARE NOW LEAVING NEW MEXICO — LAND OF ENCHANTMENT'. Texas State Line sign visible further ahead. Hazy sky.

'Welcome to Texas — Drive Friendly, The Texas Way' state welcome sign on I-40, with the Texas flag graphic on a green background. Highway overpass behind it. Hazy sky, red soil shoulder. Shot 22 seconds after the 'Leaving New Mexico' sign.
Exit 15 sign for Ivy Road near Amarillo. Overcast dusty sky, dry scrubland. A small dust devil kicking up to the right of the sign. Texas Panhandle energy.

Gray County Rest Area at night — green-lit grass and cedar shrubs in the foreground, dark storm clouds on the horizon with a reddish-brown glow. Not a famous place. Not on anyone's itinerary. Two hours and six photos anyway.

Looking out from the rest area across the Texas Panhandle at night — green-lit shrubs in the foreground, I-40 highway lights blazing on the left horizon, dark roiling storm sky above. Shot over Serenity's hood.
Heavily blurred night sky shot at Gray County — dark storm clouds with diffuse greenish light below, soft bokeh from camera movement or rain. Nearly abstract.
Texas star monument at night — triangular concrete structure with a lone star cutout, lit in blue from below. Bare trees and shrubs framing it. Green lawn.
Texas star monument — second angle, slightly wider. Blue uplighting on the white concrete structure, lone star visible. Green grass, night sky.

Gray County Rest Area's large triangular concrete Texas star monument lit in blue from below — the full wedge-shaped structure visible with the lone star cutout near the top, shrubs and a bare tree in the foreground, a light pole to the right. Shot 2 seconds after the previous frame.
Long exposure at Gray County Rest Area — car headlights leaving a streak of white and red through the frame. Rest area A-frame structure visible at top, stone wall below. Yucca plant lit green.
Second long exposure at Gray County — same setup, a faster car produces a shorter, more compact light trail. A-frame canopy and stone wall.
Texas storm at Gray County — shot from the rest area looking out at the plains. Massive dark cloud bank filling the sky, green-lit grass and cedar shrubs in the foreground, chain-link fence visible.
Memphis Bass Pro Shops Pyramid — massive dark glass pyramid on the riverfront, shot from the I-40 bridge crossing the Mississippi into Tennessee. An Infiniti QX80 in the adjacent lane.

location: El Dorado County, CA (Sierra Nevada) — DASHCAM
description: Dashcam footage (VIOFO A119 V3, BF3126) descending US-50 eastbound through the Sierra Nevada — granite rock face on left, evergreen trees above, two cars ahead, a blue alpine lake visible in the distant valley. 46 MPH. The dashcam caught the Sierra crossing the phone didn't.

location: El Dorado County, CA (Sierra Nevada) — DASHCAM
description: Second dashcam clip from the same Sierra Nevada descent on US-50 eastbound — the wagon train mentioned on the CMS sign, heading west over the summit, visible from the eastbound lanes.

location: Bonneville Salt Flats area, UT — GOPRO
description: GoPro video of driving a badly deteriorated road across a flat desert basin — crumbling asphalt and mud washes, road dead-straight to the horizon, dark storm clouds building. A dust devil spinning in the distance ahead. Probably the access road near the Bonneville flats.

Nighttime video looking off to the right of the highway at roughly 45 degrees — in the distance, a vast field of blinking red beacons high in the dark sky, likely wind turbines or radio towers. Eerie and mesmerizing across the flat Nebraska plains.

Second nighttime video of the same field of blinking red beacons off to the right of the highway — shot 9 seconds later, the sea of synchronized flashing lights still filling the darkness. Wind turbines or radio towers; still not certain which.

location: Millers Rest Stop, Esmeralda County, NV — VIDEO
description: Video of the star session at Millers Rest Stop — utility pole silhouetted against the star-filled sky, the Milky Way visible, bright headlights from a passing vehicle blazing on the right edge. The stills captured moments; this is the full Nevada desert night.

Video of an oversized load being escorted by a highway patrol vehicle on a desert two-lane road in the Mojave — the load completely tarp-covered on a heavy hauler, escort vehicle ahead. Wide open desert.
Second video clip from the same Mojave Desert road session — companion footage to the oversized load escort clip.
Third video clip from the same Mojave Desert road session.

Video from the canyon overlook near Green River, UT — the photographer's shadow falls across the red desert foreground, a Swift Trucking semi tiny on the road far below in the canyon. The scale of the landscape.

location: Gray County Rest Area, TX — VIDEO
description: Night video at Gray County Rest Area — the rest area's distinctive metal cantilevered A-frame shelter structures visible, a distant vehicle's lights on the horizon. The companion footage to the long exposure stills.

location: Gray County Rest Area, TX — VIDEO
description: Second night video at Gray County — same rest area stone wall and A-frame pole, a semi's trailer lights visible as a faint red-and-white glow in the dark beyond.

location: Gray County Rest Area, TX — VIDEO
description: Third night video at Gray County Rest Area — companion clip shot at the same time, featuring cool lightning flashing in the distance across the Texas Panhandle sky.

location: Gray County Rest Area, TX — VIDEO
description: Late-night video at Gray County — blurred lens flare and swirling light from a passing vehicle or rest area light. The first frame is nearly abstract.
Abstract long-exposure night shot at Gray County — a thin diagonal streak of lightning across the top of the frame, the rest area light blooming into a curved arc on the right. Nearly abstract.

Second abstract lightning long-exposure at Gray County, 14 seconds later — nearly identical to the previous frame, another lightning streak at the top, rest area light arc on the right. Shot just before the companion video.

Looking out from Serenity's driver seat across the Texas Panhandle at midnight — I-40 visible on a slight rise in the background with red taillights, grassy scrubland in the foreground, storm sky above. Shot over the car's hood.

location: Virginia state line (I-81 northbound, Bristol area)
description: Blurry nighttime windshield shot at highway speed — the 'Welcome to Virginia' state sign illuminated on the right, blue highway guide signs ahead, light fog on the glass. I-81, ~3am, nine thousand miles behind. Charlottesville is 45 minutes east. The coordinate system has been adjusted.
